routes.title: From Dhāt al-Kursī to al-Jady to True North and the Qibla

walkthrough.instruction: Start in the north with Dhāt al-Kursī: five bright stars in a W or M. Learn its shape first; it is your way in to al-Jady.
Next to it is Kawkabā al-Firq. Its bright star, al-Abyaḍ, is one of the stars the anwāʾ writers say lead the eye to al-Jady.
Now trace from the middle star of Dhāt al-Kursī towards the pole. Follow the line until you reach al-Jady. The line is a UFUQ teaching aid, not a historical figure.
This is al-Jady. Learn its place well: every route in UFUQ ends here, and from it you find True North.
Drop straight down from al-Jady to the horizon. That point on the ground is True North. al-Jady is the star; True North is the direction below it.
Face True North, then turn clockwise along the horizon by the Qibla bearing of this place. The arc shows the turn; the end of the arc is the Qibla.

routes.title: From Banāt Naʿsh to al-Jady to True North and the Qibla

walkthrough.instruction: Start with Banāt Naʿsh al-Kubrā: four stars make the bier and three daughters walk behind it. Learn this shape first.

Take the two stars at the end of the bier farthest from the daughters, and continue their line out of the box. Follow it to al-Jady. This pointer line is a modern UFUQ teaching aid; the anwāʾ texts do not state it.
Around al-Jady wheel al-Farqadān, the two leading stars of the lesser Banāt Naʿsh. The group runs from this bright pair to al-Jady, its last daughter.
This is al-Jady. Learn its place well: every route in UFUQ ends here, and from it you find True North.
Drop straight down from al-Jady to the horizon. That point on the ground is True North. al-Jady is the star; True North is the direction below it.
Face True North, then turn clockwise along the horizon by the Qibla bearing of this place. The arc shows the turn; the end of the arc is the Qibla.
